item.title: Re: The Bone Seer
item.content:encoded:
Hey there! Thank you so much for taking the time to go through the concept. I'm glad you like the core. Allow me to address some of the points you made.

+ My feedback
- Collapse

I really like this idea of reading the bones but I am unconvinced about the entire thing centred around a vague K-class event. That's no way to build stakes.

I'm trying to go for the idea that the SCP believes it, with the Foundation very much pointing out their scepticism at the validity of the information. This is not at all what the skip would be centred around. It'd serve to introduce the idea that the use of its abilities has shifted its worldview considerably (I mean, even in real life, we have people believing in various apocalypses), with further interviews reinforcing it. However, if you still think that wouldn't work, I get it. Some ideas from the top of my head could be the SCP worried about something/someone "corrupting the Song of the world" and wanting help from the Foundation, but that might be too vague. My (way back) original idea was the SCP being fascinated by the paranormal and wanting to assist and work in the Foundation, but I feared that would be too X-many - something I was terrified of getting close to.

also not convinced that being sure the world would end would then lead to these results… like maybe the cooperation, but why would it make the SCP apathetic about the individual lives? That's fine if you wanna make them cold towards individual lives, but it doesn't make much sense this would be the reason personally.

I was thinking it would be along the lines of "if everyone is going to be dead soon, no reason to get attached or care", or how in an apocalyptic scenario, which the SCP believes in, you'd not get too close to people as they could die at any moment. Still, it could easily be changed to a personality trait gained from being in contact with so many memories, including those of deaths.

I don't think experiment logs are the way to go here. Instead, you could summarize what research was done with the results and then unpack them in conversations or observation reports from the researchers.

I probably worded that part badly since that's what I was trying to go for. The first set of logs would be with the SCP - Foundation giving it various bones and seeing how much info it can gain from them, experimenting with the species of the bones, how old they are, how mundane they are, as well as how accurately the SCP can glean information by cross-referencing the info. The second set of logs would be D-class being given the "charms" and observing how they handle it - a normal person being exposed to memories of, say, a horse, or a murder victim. Also what psychological traits influence how the "charms" affect people (ie. how does someone with would aphantasia deal with having different memories)

I think some unpacking of the actual anomaly would be more interesting than the focus on some vague end of the world.

Again, I think I just phrased it really badly since the other gentleperson above also got that impression. The K-class is by no means the focus of the skip - it's there to explain why the SCP turned in to the Foundation and what motivates it, but beyond the Foundation expressing strong scepticism towards these claims and introducing the idea of the SCP being affected by its abilities, that's it. The meat of the story would very much be talking to the SCP and seeing how its abilities work on it and others.

Please, let me know if any of these replies convinced you/better explained about some part of the skip, or if you're still not sold about some of them working, so I can start thinking of ways to change and modify the concepts. Again, thank you very much for taking the time!

The SCP is motivated by a zealous belief that a K-class scenario is coming soon, though it doesn't know when or how, and the details it describes do not match any known K-class scenarios.

I really like this idea of reading the bones but I am unconvinced about the entire thing centered around a vague K-class event. That's no way to build stakes.

I think this could work without the vague threat, make it something a bit more grounded… like the Seer is worried about being hunted by something or someone (but don't be vague, be mysterious), while you sell it with how upset/scared they are and are looking for security in containment. (this is just an idea, you don't have to take the suggestion of course)

This belief does however leave it completely cold and apathetic to individual lives, including its own, as well as highly cooperative with the Foundation, believing it will be necessary to try and piece the world together after the cataclysm.

also not convinced that being sure the world would end would then lead to these results… like maybe the cooperation, but why would it make the SCP apathetic about the individual lives? That's fine if you wanna make them cold towards individual lives, but it doesn't make much sense this would be the reason personally.

can then turn to the experiment logs to see how various test subjects deal with having the memories of others

Also not really sold on this idea, I don't think experiment logs is the way to go here. Instead you could summarize what research was done with the results and then unpack them in conversations or observation reports from the researchers.

Overall, I like the idea of the core anomaly… but I think some unpacking of the actual anomaly would be more interesting than the focus on some vague end of the world. Most of the compelling SCPs I have read have not had such HUGE stakes. I think this would work better with a more grounded relatable story about a person who can see into weird shit and how its affected them… Maybe some of the history of the practice, where this person has been/where they've used it before, and some unpacking of their psychological status as a result.

item.title: Re: The Bone Seer
item.content:encoded: Hey there! I'm really glad you like the idea. I should point out that the K-class scenario is a claim of the SCP, not something we know will happen. The Foundation points out that the scenario as described doesn't match anything they know about and the details the SCP provides are scarce, reinforcing the idea that the SCP's mind could be somewhat confused by the number of memories it holds.

item.title: Re: The Bone Seer
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the absolutely haunting image of someone singing with my bones.
I really like this idea, the SCP is quite unique but I don't know about the narrative. Honestly K-class scenarios are getting overused and rarely work for me, specially when it is shrouded in mystery as it is here. I feel like you should go ahead and tell what this scenario is or find another reason for her to submit to the Foundation. Either way it is a nice concept and I would love to see it going forward on the wiki.

item.title: The Bone Seer
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP document with a large focus on interview/experiment logs

Elevator Pitch: A woman capable of gaining information about others by handling their bones (as well as passing the information on) turns herself in to the Foundation, motivated by a steadfast belief that a K-class scenario is coming.

Central Narrative: After an unrelated incident in which an agent was KIA, the SCP, then working as a mortician, becomes aware of the Foundation via handling the agent's bones and shortly after turns itself in to the Foundation. After the Foundation ensures it's not a GOI agent, the SCP is taken in.

The SCP is able to gain information through physical contact with the bones of others (by what it claims is "listening to the Song") and carve the bones with various occult symbols to allow others to similarly glean the information. It claims its abilities are not born/naturally occurring but rather were taught to it by its grandmother. As the SCP has no living family, the info can not be verified. No attempts to recreate the scrimshaw by using the same symbols or teach others to "listen to the Song" have been successful.

+ show block
– hide block

The SCP is motivated by a zealous belief that a K-class scenario is coming soon, though it doesn't know when or how, and the details it describes do not match any known K-class scenarios. It's unclear whether the claim is valid or merely religious - possibly a side effect of the repeated use of its abilities, as it can sometimes have problems distinguishing its own memories from the ones gained via its abilities. This belief does however leave it completely cold and apathetic to individual lives, including its own, as well as highly cooperative with the Foundation, believing it will be necessary to try and piece the world together after the cataclysm.

The Foundation is left trying to find out how reliable is the SCP itself and its claims, as well the extent of its abilities to gain and pass information and whether it could be useful, though it remains wary of possible memetic agents.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The reader is left trying to figure out exactly how the SCP works and thinks, how sane it is, and can then turn to the experiment logs to see how various test subjects deal with having the memories of others, sometimes not even human.

Additional Notes: I can provide additional details in comments, but I'm currently at the exact word limit.
